# On-Call Handoff — Gateway 503s (2026-03-14)

**Status at time of writing: ACTIVE, unmitigated.** Logs end 03:59:27Z with the fault still firing and the wait queue still growing. Assume it is ongoing.

## TL;DR

Roll back **dep-4471** (gateway config). Set `gateway.pool.perRequest` back to `false`. Config-only change, ~2 min to apply.

## Root cause

dep-4471 flipped the gateway to open a new upstream connection per request instead of reusing pooled ones. The pool is 20 slots; demand immediately exceeded it and never came back down. Every 503 is a gateway-side connection-acquisition failure — **no upstream ever returned an error.**

Evidence chain, all from `logs/gateway.log`:

```
02:12:12.820Z INFO  config  reload requested by deploy pipeline, generation 118 -> 119
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config  generation 119 applied: 3 keys changed
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.pool.perRequest: false -> true      <-- this one
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.timeout.upstreamMs: 2000 -> 2500
02:13:41.234Z INFO  config    gateway.log.sampleRate: 1.0 -> 1.0
02:14:14.920Z WARN  pool    req-07400 /v1/checkout acquire slow: waited 100ms for a connection
02:14:18.972Z ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
02:14:18.972Z ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```

**38 seconds** from config applied to first 503. Corroborating signal at 03:02:30.904Z:

```
WARN pool connection churn: 4180 opens in the last 5m, baseline is 40
```

~100× the normal connection-open rate — exactly what per-request connections produce.

The pool never recovers and the queue grows without bound, +20 waiters per 5 min, linear:

| time | in_use | idle | waiting |
|---|---|---|---|
| 02:10:58 | 10 | 10 | 0 |
| 02:15:58 | 20 | 0 | 12 |
| 02:30:58 | 20 | 0 | 72 |
| 03:40:58 | 20 | 0 | 112 |
| 03:55:58 | 20 | 0 | 172 |

This will not self-heal. It needs the revert.

## Impact window

**Start: 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z** (first 503)
**End: not yet — still failing at 03:59:27.974Z**, last line of log
**Duration so far: 1h 45m (105 min)**

Post-onset traffic on this node, 636 requests:

- **530 × 503 (83.3%)**, 106 × 200 (16.7%)
- Paired 1:1 with 530 `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED` — one pool error per 503, no other error type in the file

By endpoint, post-onset:

| endpoint | requests | 503s | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| /v1/checkout | 106 | 106 | **100%** |
| /v1/cart | 106 | 106 | **100%** |
| /v1/session | 106 | 106 | **100%** |
| /v1/orders | 106 | 106 | **100%** |
| /v1/catalog/search | 106 | 106 | **100%** |
| /health | 106 | 0 | **0%** |

**Every revenue path is at 100% failure.** Checkout and cart have not served a successful request since 02:14. Failures are spread evenly across all four upstreams (83–84% each: accounts, billing, catalog, orders), which confirms it's the gateway, not any one service.

Latency on failing requests drifts upward with the queue: 659ms at onset → 749ms at 03:06 → 850ms at 03:59.

## ⚠️ Detection gap — read this before trusting dashboards

**`/health` returns 200 for the entire incident.** It does not take a pooled connection, so it stayed green while 100% of real traffic failed. Load-balancer health checks would have kept this node in rotation the whole time.

That's why the page was late:

```
03:21:05.282Z WARN ops paged on-call: error_rate 5m avg is 71%
```

**67 minutes after onset.** Do not use `/health` to verify the fix — check `/v1/checkout` directly.

(`/v1/profile` is also misleading: post-onset it stops emitting access lines entirely and appears only in `acquire slow` warnings, with waits climbing 155ms → 890ms. It's degraded, not healthy.)

## Rollback

**Revert dep-4471** — `gateway`, 02:12–02:14Z, a.novak, *"config: connection-per-request for pool isolation"*.

Minimum safe action: `gateway.pool.perRequest` → `false`. The other two keys in generation 119 are not implicated — `sampleRate` was a no-op (1.0 → 1.0), and `upstreamMs` 2000 → 2500 is not the failure mode, though reverting the whole generation is cleaner if your tooling does it atomically.

**Do not roll back these** — ruled out:

- **dep-4472** (billing-svc, 02:41) and **dep-4473** (catalog-svc, 03:20) both shipped *after* onset. Neither changed the failure rate; `waiting` climbs at a flat +20/5min straight through both.
- **dep-4469** (accounts-svc, rate limit on /v1/session) — would show 429s, not `ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED`, and all five endpoints fail equally, not just session.
- **dep-4468** (catalog-svc, 22:04 prior day) — 4h before, clean traffic in between.

**Verify after revert:** pool `waiting` should return toward 0 and `in_use` off the 20 ceiling in the next `pool stats` sample (they're emitted every ~5 min), and `/v1/checkout` should return 200.

## Second, separate issue — do not conflate

`logs/worker.log` shows **zero failures**: 1,080 jobs, all `finished ok`, throughput flat at 60 per 10 min, worker pool idle at `size=8 in_use=1 idle=7 waiting=0` in all 18 samples. The gateway fault did not touch the workers.

**But worker job latency is degrading independently:** 327ms → 2,197ms average, climbing **exactly +110ms per 10 minutes**, ruler-straight from the first line of the log (01:00) to the last (03:59). No inflection at 02:14 — the climb was already 74 minutes old when the gateway broke, so the two are unrelated. `db_wait` is flat at 5.0ms in every bucket, so it's not the database; the time is going somewhere inside the worker process. All six job types affected identically.

Nothing is failing from this yet, but it's unbounded and still climbing. **File it separately — it does not block or get fixed by the gateway rollback.**

Lead for whoever picks it up: dep-4470 shipped to the worker at 00:48–00:55Z and worker.log starts at 01:00, five minutes later — so there is no pre-deploy baseline in this file and the trend is already underway on line one. dep-4470 is the natural suspect on timing but **is not confirmed**; you need worker logs from before 00:48 to tell whether the climb starts at the deploy.

Unrelated, single occurrence, self-flagged as known:
```
02:36:22.838Z WARN db slow query 1.9s: SELECT * FROM orders WHERE status = ? — unindexed scan, known issue OPS-2210
```

## Caveat on scope

`gateway.log` header says **`node-3 of 3`**. This is one node's view. The reload came from the deploy pipeline, so nodes 1 and 2 almost certainly received generation 119 too — but I cannot confirm that from these files. **Check the other two nodes before declaring the blast radius**, and make sure the revert reaches all three.

---

I kept this as chat output rather than writing a file, since I don't know where your incident docs live — say the word and I'll drop it at a path you name.
